Trace the Lineage of a Variable Through the Derivation Graph

Source: R/trace_validate.R
trace_lineage.Rd

Given a single variable, walks the derivation graph behind trace_chains() and returns its lineage: either every upstream source it derives from (its full ancestry) or every downstream variable that derives from it (its dependents). This is the general path query over the graph; trace_impact() is the special case of downstream dependents of a source variable.

Usage

trace_lineage(
  trace_model,
  node,
  direction = c("upstream", "downstream"),
  adam_derivations = NULL,
  max_depth = Inf
)

Arguments

trace_model

A trace_model from build_trace_model().

node

A single variable identifier as "DATASET.VARIABLE", for example "ADSL.AGE".

direction

One of "upstream" (sources the node derives from, the default) or "downstream" (variables that derive from the node).

adam_derivations

Optional data.frame of ADaM-to-ADaM derivations with columns from_dataset, from_var, to_dataset, to_var, as in trace_chains().

max_depth

Optional maximum number of hops to report. Inf (the default) reports the full transitive lineage.

Value

A tibble with one row per related variable: dataset, variable, role, depth (hops from the queried node), and path (a readable derivation path reading outward from the node). Rows are ordered nearest first. Zero rows means the node has no lineage in the requested direction. The result carries "node" and "direction" attributes.

Details

A directed edge runs from a derived variable to its source. trace_lineage() follows those edges in one of two directions from the queried node:

  • direction = "upstream" follows edges forward, toward sources, and returns the transitive set of everything the variable is derived from, down to the SDTM variables that ground it.

  • direction = "downstream" follows edges in reverse and returns the transitive set of variables that depend on it.

ADaM-to-ADaM derivations are included when supplied through adam_derivations, exactly as in trace_chains(), so multi-step lineage is captured. Each related variable is reported once, at its shortest distance from the queried node, with a readable path that reads outward from the node. Circular references are handled and do not loop.

See also

trace_impact() for downstream impact of a source variable, trace_chains() for per-variable chain summaries, validate_trace_graph() for structural integrity checks.

Examples

adam <- data.frame(
  dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"), variable = c("AGE", "AAGE"),
  label = c("Age", "Analysis Age")
)
sdtm <- data.frame(dataset = "DM", variable = "AGE", label = "Age")
map <- data.frame(
  adam_dataset = "ADSL", adam_var = "AGE",
  sdtm_domain = "DM", sdtm_var = "AGE", confidence = 1
)
tm <- build_trace_model(adam, sdtm, mapping = map)
deriv <- data.frame(
  from_dataset = "ADAE", from_var = "AAGE",
  to_dataset = "ADSL", to_var = "AGE"
)

# Where does ADAE.AAGE come from?
trace_lineage(tm, "ADAE.AAGE", "upstream", adam_derivations = deriv)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   dataset variable role  depth path                           
#>   <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <int> <chr>                          
#> 1 ADSL    AGE      adam      1 ADAE.AAGE -> ADSL.AGE          
#> 2 DM      AGE      sdtm      2 ADAE.AAGE -> ADSL.AGE -> DM.AGE

# What depends on DM.AGE?
trace_lineage(tm, "DM.AGE", "downstream", adam_derivations = deriv)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   dataset variable role  depth path                           
#>   <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <int> <chr>                          
#> 1 ADSL    AGE      adam      1 DM.AGE -> ADSL.AGE             
#> 2 ADAE    AAGE     adam      2 DM.AGE -> ADSL.AGE -> ADAE.AAGE
